newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: CarnaudMetalbox's SIEM gets Abidjan list.
newsitem.headline: CarnaudMetalbox's SIEM gets Abidjan list.

text.p: Ivory Coast's leading producer of cans and metal packaging, Societe Ivoirienne d'Emballages Metalliques (SIEM), was formally listed on the Abidjan bourse on Thursday after the partial privatisation of the government's 10 percent stake.
Only 59 percent of the 1.15 billion CFA francs ($2 million) of shares on offer were taken up by the public.
SIEM is 85-percent owned by CarnaudMetalbox, itself now a subsidiary of Crown Cork and Seal of the U.S. The other five percent is held by a non-profit-making Ivorian body.
The shares were officially listed at 29,500 CFA francs on the bourse's Second Market. They will begin trading at the next session on June 10.
The Abidjan bourse only trades on Tuesdays and Thursdays for half an hour each session.
SIEM had sales of just under 21 billion CFA francs in the year to end-September 1996 and managing director Alain Escat said roughly the same was expected for 1996/97.
